To determine who caused the September 11, 2001 attacks, we look at the historical and investigative consensus established by the official 9/11 Commission Report, as well as extensive international intelligence investigations. 

Step 1: Review the historical consensus and the findings of the bipartisan 9/11 Commission. The attacks were planned and executed by the militant Islamist terrorist organization Al-Qaeda.
Step 2: Identify the leader and operatives. Al-Qaeda, led by Osama bin Laden, directed the hijacking of four commercial airplanes, resulting in the tragic deaths of nearly 3,000 people in New York City, Washington, D.C., and Shanksville, Pennsylvania.
Step 3: Evaluate the options. Options (A), (D), (E), and (F) represent conspiracy theories regarding the attacks, while options (B) and (G) incorrectly implicate foreign states that were not responsible. Option (C) correctly identifies the terrorist group responsible according to all credible evidence and historical records.

Final answer: C
